parts.What happened: I find revenue fell estimated ~$172K CAD (3.9%) and operating profit fell 21% from 2024 to 2025.
parts.Why: I find broadly steady average charges; 55% of the revenue decline came from 26% fewer root-canal services, averaging estimated $1,347 CAD/service. I find rent and salaried staff costs unchanged, so costs fell more slowly than revenue.
parts.What it's worth: I estimate recovering 36 of the 72 lost services (50%) could add estimated ~$48K CAD/year in service revenue, before extra costs.
parts.What to do: I would check referrals sent elsewhere, dentist availability and accepted-but-unbooked treatment plans.
parts.How to measure: I would track root-canal services per month and the treatment-plan acceptance rate.

parts.What happened: I find the no-show rate is 9.3% for 30+-day bookings versus 3.0% for bookings under 7 days, about 3.1 times as high.
parts.Why: I find the same rising pattern in 3 of 3 branches, so I would test whether reminders and confirmations improve attendance.
parts.What it's worth: I estimate matching the 7–29-day rate could retain about 230 visits/year and add estimated ~$57K CAD/year in service revenue, before extra costs.
parts.What to do: I would pilot a reminder 7 days before care and a reply-to-confirm 48 hours before care at one branch. I would have staff review unconfirmed slots before offering them to a short-notice waitlist.
parts.How to measure: I would track the no-show rate for 30+-day bookings and slots refilled against a comparison branch.

parts.What happened: I find estimated ~$447K CAD of estimated ~$633K CAD owed is over 90 days old at 2025-12-31.
parts.Why: I would check whether insurer delays, patient balances or billing errors explain the older bills. I note an estimated ~$314K CAD timing lift in 2024 cash because tracked unpaid operating bills start at zero.
parts.What it's worth: I estimate recovering 25% of 91–180-day bills could release estimated ~$17K CAD in cash, before collection costs. I would not count this as new service revenue or subtract unpaid bills from profit.
parts.What to do: I would run a collections process for 60–180-day bills (estimated ~$89K CAD), classifying each balance as insurer, patient or billing-error work.
parts.How to measure: I would track days to collect and the unpaid balance over 90 days.

findings.title: Prioritize Maple for the reminder pilot

parts.What happened: I find Maple has a 6.3% no-show rate versus 4.6% at Harbour; the difference is statistically significant (two-sided p < 0.001).
parts.Why: I also find Maple above Harbour within every booking lead-time band, so I would investigate its confirmation workflow.
parts.What it's worth: I estimate matching Harbour could retain about 100 visits/year and add estimated ~$25K CAD/year in service revenue, before extra costs. I do not add this to the group reminder opportunity because they overlap.
parts.What to do: I would prioritize Maple for the reminder and confirmation pilot.
parts.How to measure: I would track Maple's no-show rate and its change against Harbour, split by booking lead time.
